rulesIntro: Expert GFC Cup 2026 · 9-a-side Football Tournament · Tournament Rules and Regulations

rules.title: Teams & Format
rules.text:
16 teams have been finalised for this tournament.
The teams will be divided into four (4) groups of four (4) teams.
The top two (2) teams (winners and runners-up) from each group will progress to the knockout round (quarterfinals), leading to the Grand Final.

rules.title: Awards
rules.text: Prize money, trophies and medals will be awarded to the champions and runners up.

rules.title: Fixtures & Venue
rules.text:
The venue for the event will be Mitchelton Football Club, Teralba Park, Everton Park, QLD 4053.
Parking is available at the Football ground.

rules.title: Tournament Commencement
rules.text:
The tournament will be held on the 5th of July 2026 (Sunday).
It will be a full day event commencing from 7.30am and ending at 7.00pm.
Teams are required to be at the field by 7:30am.
The first games are scheduled to kick off at 8:00am.

rules.title: Referees
rules.text: Referees will be provided on the day.

rules.title: Registration
rules.text:
All players must be registered before they are eligible to play.
A player can only register and play for one team throughout the whole tournament.
A separate players registration form (team sheet) has to be completed and submitted to the organiser, Gurkha FC (GFC) on gurkhafc2008@yahoo.com, preferably a day before the tournament. Notwithstanding, the team sheet must be submitted to GFC's technical committee 15 minutes prior to the team's first group game.
The team sheet must contain the full name, jersey number and signature for all players.
Following submission of the registration form, no changes to the registered players in the team sheet will be allowed for the duration of the tournament.

rules.title: Player Eligibility
rules.text:
This tournament is only open to Nepalese and Bhutanese teams, with players of Nepalese and Bhutanese heritage who are residing in Australia.
Any team who breaches this rule will be disqualified from the tournament regardless of their standing in the tournament.

rules.title: Registration Fee
rules.text: A registration fee of AUD$800.00 is to be paid to the organiser (GFC) prior to the start of the tournament. Payment details have been sent out in the earlier invitation letter.

rules.title: Laws of the Game & Offside
rules.text:
Matches are played in conformity with the Laws of the Game promulgated by the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and published by FIFA.
The offside rule does not apply.

rules.title: Players
rules.text:
ALL players must be registered, wear shin pads and wear the team colour jersey with number to be able to play in a match. No jewellery is allowed to be worn during play.
A maximum of 16 players may be registered in the team sheet; a minimum of nine (9) is required to form a complete team.
A minimum of six (6) players is required to start a game.
Nine players per side, including the goalkeeper, are allowed on the field during the course of the match.
Up to seven (7) substitutes can be named by each team in each complete game.
A player is only allowed to play for the team they are registered to. No player may play for two teams registered in the tournament. Any team who breaches this rule will face expulsion from the tournament, regardless of their standing in the tournament.

rules.title: Substitution of Players
rules.text:
There will be unlimited rolling substitutions.
Permission of the referee is required to substitute players.

rules.title: Fouls, Misconduct & Cards
rules.text:
The decisions made by the referee during the games are final.
Yellow card: if a player receives 2 yellow cards during a game, it warrants a red card, and the player will be sent off from the match. No replacement will be allowed. The offending player will be suspended for the next match as well.
Yellow card accumulation: a player who accumulates 5 yellow cards will be suspended following the match when the fifth (5th) yellow card is received.
Red card: no replacement will be allowed in the event a player is red-carded. The offending player will miss the following game.

rules.title: Match Time: Group Stage
rules.text:
Each group game will be a period of 12 mins per half (24 mins playing time in total), with a 3-minute break at the half.
There will be no extra time or penalty kicks in the group matches.
Players have to be on the field on time.
Every quarter of game time which a team is late for would award the opponent a 1-0 lead; and only the remaining allocated time will be played.
E.g. a team which is up to 6 minutes late (i.e. between 1min to 6min) will award the opponents a 1-0 lead (i.e. approx. a quarter of the full 24 minutes game); if the team is up to 12 minutes late, the opponent will be awarded a 2-0 lead.
A team which is absent and misses the full game would award the opponent a 4-0 victory.

rules.title: Injury & Stoppage Time
rules.text: Injury and stoppage times will be determined by the referee and added to the regulation game times at all stages of the tournament.

rules.title: Equality of Points
rules.text:
If two or more teams are equal on points on completion of all the matches in the group stage, the following criteria will be used to determine the rankings in the order given:
1. Goal difference in the matches among the teams in question.
2. Number of goals scored in the matches among the teams in question.
3. All else being the same, penalty kicks among the teams in question will determine their final rankings. 5 penalty takers from each team are required. If the shootout ends in a stalemate, sudden death rules apply, with both teams having equal opportunities.

rules.title: Match Time: Quarter-Finals & Semi-Finals
rules.text:
For all knockout matches, each game will be played for a period of 12 mins per half (24 mins playing time in total), with a 3-minute break at the half.
Extra time: if the result ends in a draw at the end of normal playing time, an extra time of 5 continuous minutes shall be played with no half-time. Extra time shall commence with a kick-off from the centre of the field with the teams switching sides.
Penalty shootout: if the match ends in a draw after extra time, the winners shall be determined by a penalty shootout. 5 penalty takers from each team are required. If the shootout ends in a stalemate, sudden death rules apply, with both teams having equal opportunities.
As a rule, the players remain on the field of play during breaks and at extra time, at the discretion of the referee.

rules.title: Match Time: Grand Final
rules.text:
The Grand Final will be played at 15 mins per half (30 mins playing time in total) with a 3-minute break at the half.
Extra time: if the result ends in a draw at the end of normal playing time, an extra time of a continuous 7 minutes shall be played with no half-time. Extra time shall commence with a kick-off from the centre of the field with the teams switching sides.
Penalty shootout: if the match ends in a draw after extra time, the winners shall be determined by a penalty shootout. 5 penalty takers from each team are required. If the shootout ends in a stalemate, sudden death rules apply, with both teams having equal opportunities.
As a rule, the players remain on the field of play during breaks and at extra time, at the discretion of the referee.

rules.title: Penalty Kicks
rules.text:
The referee decides the goal post that will be used for the penalty shootout.
There would be a coin toss on deciding the team who would be taking the penalty first.

rules.title: Sportsmanship & Technical Area
rules.text:
Teams and their players are to maintain sportsmanship and follow rules and regulations as set out for the tournament.
The GFC Technical Committee holds sportsmanship in high regard and expects all participating teams and players to play and behave in a respectful manner befitting their standings as participants in the tournament.
Only the on-field teams' players, managers and coaches are allowed in the technical/substitute area. Everyone else is to remain away from the technical area.
Supporters are NOT allowed in the technical/substitute area. Only the on-field teams' managers, coaches and players are allowed.
Supporters are expected to stay off the field when a game is being played. It is the responsibility of the team managers to ensure that their supporters stay off the field.

rules.title: Referees' Safety
rules.text:
The referees' decisions are final, and any on-field disputes will be handled by the referee, with all teams and players having the understanding that minor on-field disputes will occur.
"Every worker has the right to go home safe and healthy every day and every employer has the responsibility to provide a safe work environment." Likewise, the referees for the day have a right to go home safe and healthy. The referees are important officials required for the tournament to operate in a smooth and respectable manner.
In the event that a major on-field dispute occurs and the offending team/player(s)/supporter(s) compromise, or appear to compromise the safety of the referees and an unfortunate incident occurs (e.g. overwhelming and inappropriate surrounding/harassment of a referee where the referee deems his safety is in danger, physical assault), strict actions will be taken by the GFC Technical Committee on the offending team(s)/player(s) which may include:
• Immediate expulsion of the offending team(s)/player(s), regardless of their standings in the tournament.
• Offending team(s)/player(s) barred from future GFC organised tournaments for a specific period of time at the discretion of the GFC Technical Committee.
• Reporting the incident to the police.

rules.title: Dispute Lodgement Process
rules.text:
If a team believes that an opposition has infringed the rules of the tournament, a formal dispute request may be provided to the GFC Technical Committee. The dispute request shall be submitted to the GFC Technical Committee within 10 minutes upon completion of the game in which the offence occurred. No requests will be accepted after this 10-minute period has elapsed.
Dispute resolution will be handled by the GFC Technical Committee and a decision made prior to the team's next game (if applicable). The GFC Technical Committee's decision is final. Note that only serious offences will be considered and any on-field decisions by the referee are final.

rules.title: Tournament Schedule
rules.text: The tournament's schedule will be announced and provided to the participating teams closer to the date of the competition.
